- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.5+ sentiment) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.5) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts 1–2 days too late to sentiment changes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows — correct by smoothing out 3–5 day moving averages.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves — model forecasts peak too early and then drops below true value.
- High sentiment + high price history → model overconfident in upward trend — reduce forecast slope.
- Low sentiment + low price history → model underestimates risk of reversal — increase downward buffer.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.5 → model should reduce forecast variance and add hedging margin.
- Always adjust forecast downward if sentiment turns from positive to negative within 3 days.
- Forecast should not exceed 1.5x recent 18-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>1.5) and confirmed.
